name: slack-reel
title: Slack Reel
description: An inline loader read as cord paid out between two spools instead of a bar — sag encodes recent throughput, so a stalled request visibly stops paying out line and the cord goes taut on its own.
instruction: An inline loading indicator, one visual for both busy and known-progress states: a thin cord runs between two 10px spools (stroke --border) as a single quadratic SVG path whose control-point y is slack. Indeterminate mode (no `value` prop) rocks the slack on a fixed loop forever: the left spool pays out over 700ms ease-in-cubic, the right spool reels it back taut over 400ms ease-out-expo, then a short rest, repeating — this is the whole component's job while mounted, so it never sleeps. Determinate mode (`value` 0-100, controlled) derives slack from the VELOCITY of value changes, not the value itself: each update computes an instantaneous %/s rate, smoothed into a running estimate, and slack chases min(maxSlack, velocity * k) with its own settle rate — so fast throughput reads as visible sag and a request that stops sending updates (or keeps sending the same value) decays its own velocity estimate to zero within ~350ms and the cord pulls itself taut with no further prop writes at all. That's the honesty the mechanism is built around: a spinner cannot express 'stopped', a sagging line that stops paying out can. A rotation tick on each spool (stroke --foreground) counter-rotates across a bounded ~300deg sweep mapped directly from `value` (never a full turn, so the reading never wraps back on itself and ambiguates with its own start). On reaching 100 the cord snaps: an underdamped spring (zeta 0.5) pulls slack through zero with one clean overshoot wobble, then the whole cord dims to 42% opacity over ~550ms as a resting cue; passing a fresh lower `value` afterwards un-dims it and starts a new run. Geometry is pixel-real (an SVG viewBox tracked via ResizeObserver, not percentage-relative), so the same component reads correctly from a ~40x16px inline chip up to a full-width panel divider — width is entirely the caller's className, height is fixed and small. Pure SVG + a single direct-DOM rAF loop (React state only carries the announcement text); no canvas, no dependencies. Accessibility: role=progressbar with an accessible label; determinate exposes aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow, indeterminate omits all three per spec (no value to report). A visually-hidden aria-live=polite region announces 'Loading' on mount, 10%-step milestones ('40% loaded', ...) while determinate, and 'Done' on completion; a value drop after completion re-announces 'Loading' as a fresh run. prefers-reduced-motion drops the rAF loop entirely: rotation goes off (both ticks stay upright, static), the cord holds a simple three-state sag (taut at 0%, a fixed partial sag mid-run, taut again at 100% or on any indeterminate frame) with a slow 2.4s opacity pulse as the only motion, and completion still dims to rest, just instantly rather than through the spring.
